session.question: How do PAs create public value in sustainability reporting?
session.answer:
Public administrations (PAs) create public value in sustainability reporting through three linked mechanisms: preserving and disseminating public value, obtaining legitimacy and support from stakeholders, and building operational capacity. In the strategic-triangle framing, sustainability reports are not merely disclosure tools; they are instruments through which PAs communicate how they contribute to economic, social, and environmental objectives. The analysis of Italian Port Authorities shows that textual reporting can support these mechanisms by structuring non-financial information around sustainability commitments and by making public value visible to relevant audiences. (valenza2023sustainabilityreportingand chunk 1)

More broadly, PAs create public value when reporting is embedded in accountability and governance processes that promote transparency, stakeholder participation, data gathering, measurement, and communication. Such reporting can align public action with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), while involving business, investors, and civil society and maintaining central coordination to support coherent implementation. In this sense, public value arises not only from disclosure itself, but from the institutional capacity to coordinate, justify, and steer sustainability-oriented action. (abhayawansa2021accountabilityandgovernance chunk 1)

A related public-sector approach emphasizes that reporting should be planned to respond to sustainability challenges and to align disclosure with broader accountability needs. Hybrid models combining integrated reporting and the SDGs can help administrations support sustainability delivery and public value creation. (gherardi2021accountabilityandreporting chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-8e0fab5e: The excerpt says the study uses the strategic triangle framework of public value to analyze non-financial disclosures in sustainability reports of eight Italian Port Authorities. According to the abstract, public administrations (PAs) create public value through sustainability reporting by preserving and disseminating public value, obtaining legitimacy and support from stakeholders, and building operational capacity. The research examines textual content with cluster analysis and lexical correspondence analysis to understand these mechanisms. The focus is on how sustainability reporting helps PAs contribute to economic, social, and environmental goals.
From Giuseppe Valenza and Rodolfo Damiano. Sustainability reporting and public value: evidence from port authorities. Utilities Policy, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jup.2023.101508, doi:10.1016/j.jup.2023.101508.

pqac-eea4ab68: The excerpt discusses how national governments and public administrations can create value for society and the economy through their approach to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It highlights that, in the Australian Senate inquiry submissions, stakeholders emphasized transparency, stakeholder participation, data gathering, measuring, and communicating as key elements of accountability systems. It also stresses involving business, investors, and civil society, along with strong central coordination by the Office of the Prime Minister and Cabinet. The paper frames public value creation in sustainability reporting as a governance and accountability process focused on national coordination and inclusive reporting to support sustainable development.
From Subhash Abhayawansa, Carol A. Adams, and Cristina Neesham. Accountability and governance in pursuit of sustainable development goals: conceptualising how governments create value. Accounting Auditing & Accountability Journal, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1108/aaaj-07-2020-4667, doi:10.1108/aaaj-07-2020-4667.

pqac-2616684f: The paper argues that public administrations can create public value in sustainability reporting by planning accountability and reporting practices that respond to public sector challenges around sustainability. In the Emilia-Romagna Region case, the administration hybridized two recent sustainability developments—integrated reporting and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)—to support the delivery of sustainability and public value. The study focuses on Cohesion Policy Programmes as a major EU investment strategy and suggests that reporting in the public sector should not only disclose information but also align with broader sustainability objectives and public-sector accountability needs.
From Lodovico Gherardi, Anna Maria Linsalata, Enrico Deidda Gagliardo, and Rebecca Levy Orelli. Accountability and reporting for sustainability and public value: challenges in the public sector. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13031097, doi:10.3390/su13031097.

pqac-dd5df5bc: The excerpt is about a 2023 paper on modeling effective interaction between society and public administration for sustainable development policy. It says the study examines how public administration and society interact to support sustainable development, using graphical structural analysis to build a hierarchical data model of processes for effective interaction. The paper focuses on a specific region (the Cotswolds, England) and discusses public administration’s strong cooperation in sustainable development. However, it does not directly discuss sustainability reporting or explain how PAs create public value through reporting.
From Myroslav Kryshtanovych, Iryna Kiyanka, Vasyl OSTAPIAK, Lesia Kornat, and Oleksandr Kuchyk. Modeling effective interaction between society and public administration for sustainable development policy. International Journal of Sustainable Development and Planning, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.18280/ijsdp.180827, doi:10.18280/ijsdp.180827.

pqac-000edc45: The excerpt is a bibliographic abstract for a systematic literature review on values, public administration, and sustainability, not a direct study of sustainability reporting mechanisms. It states that values influence actions, judgments, and leaders’ decision-making, contributing to more sustainable performance. The paper analyzes 2,038 Scopus articles and identifies key themes such as sustainability, CSR, sustainable development, innovation, and leadership, as well as the main public administration areas studied. It also notes that the results include how studies are framed in sustainability pillars and the types of values referred to, but it does not explain specific ways public administrations create public value in sustainability reporting.
From Isabel Cristina Panziera Marques, João Leitão, Alba Carvalho, and Dina Pereira. Public administration and values oriented to sustainability: a systematic approach to the literature. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13052566, doi:10.3390/su13052566.
